scope: Local authority evidence for round 2; no execution or challenge-coverage result is asserted.

priority_interpretation.meaning_of_colored_list_cells: origin/proposer, explicitly defined by Windows B4

user_reported_organiser_guarantee.statement: The user reports organisers said every challenge can be solved using the main tools.
user_reported_organiser_guarantee.document_corroboration: No all-challenges-sufficient guarantee found in the inspected workbook cells or PDF text layer.
user_reported_organiser_guarantee.use: Keep as a preparation premise; do not claim it was independently validated or printed in these sources.

formatting.tool_name_bold: All 200 approved name cells use identical style 8 (font 13, bold Arial 10, no fill).
formatting.other_emphasis: Dark blue header fill is structural. Orange/red merged headers are AI restrictions; red Kali B6 is the operational caveat. Gray Kali H text is a hidden raw-source column. URL blue/underline denotes hyperlinks.

wb-origin-legend.text: The 'List' column shows the origin of each tool: 1 = proposed by TrendMicro, 2 = added at the request of participants.
wb-origin-legend.meaning: List numbers identify who proposed the tool; no priority ranking is stated.

wb-windows-availability.text: Tools listed below are pre-approved and will already be available on the competition PCs.
wb-windows-availability.meaning: All 39 Windows-sheet entries are pre-approved and promised available; no operational guarantee is stated.

wb-windows-ai-limit.text: Installation of AI-related libraries or tools is not permitted for any tool that supports adding additional libraries or sub-tools (e.g. Python).
wb-windows-ai-limit.meaning: AI-related libraries and sub-tools are prohibited.

wb-browser-only.text: Note: Several exercises require only a web browser — no additional tool installation needed for those.
wb-browser-only.meaning: Several exercises require only a browser; this is not a statement about every challenge.

wb-kali-availability.text: Tools installed on the Kali Linux (AWS) environment provided to all teams. All tools on this list were added at the request of participants.
wb-kali-availability.meaning: All Kali-sheet entries are described as installed in the shared Kali environment and participant-requested.

wb-kali-ai-limit.text: Installation of AI-related libraries or tools is not permitted for any tool that supports adding additional libraries or sub-tools (e.g. Python).
wb-kali-ai-limit.meaning: AI-related libraries and sub-tools are prohibited.

wb-kali-best-effort.text: Tools were installed on a best-effort basis. Operation of each tool is not guaranteed.
wb-kali-best-effort.meaning: Kali installation is best-effort and operation is explicitly not guaranteed.

wb-python-libraries.text: Libraries may be added freely EXCEPT any AI/ML-related library (e.g. no LLM, machine-learning, or generative-AI frameworks).
wb-python-libraries.meaning: Python libraries may be added except AI/ML-related ones.

wb-uv-libraries.text: Same rule as Python 3 — any library OK except AI/ML-related packages
wb-uv-libraries.meaning: uv follows the same Python library restriction.

wb-without-unapproved-tools.text: The challenges can be solved without it.
wb-without-unapproved-tools.meaning: 38 per-tool rejection reasons establish those named tools are not necessary. They do not identify the blue group as an exhaustive sufficient set.

pdf-installed.section: Software and Tools / Installed by the organizer
pdf-installed.text: Approved Tool List software; Approved Tool Request submissions; Latest version at the time installation starts (mid-October)
pdf-installed.meaning: Both organiser-proposed and participant-requested approved tools are covered.
pdf-installed.text_form: Selected bullet/heading excerpts joined with semicolons; whitespace normalized.

pdf-libraries.section: Software and Tools / You may install
pdf-libraries.text: Libraries; Dependencies; Plugins; Packages; as long as the software is not related to Generative AI
pdf-libraries.meaning: The PDF allows non-generative-AI additions; workbook wording additionally excludes AI/ML-related libraries.
pdf-libraries.text_form: Selected bullet/heading excerpts joined with semicolons; whitespace normalized.

pdf-standalone-approval.text: Standalone applications not on the approved list require organizer approval
pdf-standalone-approval.meaning: Library/package allowance is not blanket approval for standalone applications.

pdf-commercial-license.text: Software that requires a commercial license (e.g., IDA) cannot be used with a personal license
pdf-commercial-license.meaning: A personal commercial license does not authorize use; reiterated in FAQ page 21.

pdf-shared-environment.text: All teams use the same environment
pdf-shared-environment.meaning: Equal availability is stated, not all-challenge sufficiency.

pdf-kali-defender.text: Tools that Defender may detect are installed on Kali Linux, so Defender will not detect them.
pdf-kali-defender.meaning: The question names Hayabusa/Sigma rules, Metasploit payloads and mimikatz; page 4 says the same.

pdf-version-time.text: Installation starts in mid-October, and the latest version at that time is installed.
pdf-version-time.meaning: Version authority refers to installation time, not necessarily the latest current upstream release.

pdf-no-uploads.section: FAQ ① Tools and Online Services
pdf-no-uploads.text: Online services that require uploading challenge files are not allowed.
pdf-no-uploads.meaning: Online examples include Aperi'Solve; the approved local Kali installation does not waive the upload rule.

pdf-ai-policy.text: Generative AI is prohibited; You may NOT use AI to Generate solutions, code or scripts; Analyze challenge content
pdf-ai-policy.meaning: This is an event rule; it is not a statement that the tool list can solve every challenge.
pdf-ai-policy.text_form: Selected bullet/heading excerpts joined with semicolons; whitespace normalized.
